title: Patrick Stewart, Legendary Star Trek Actor, Dies at 86
paragraphs: Patrick Stewart, the classically trained British actor who found worldwide fame as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in "Star Trek: The Next Generation" and as Professor Charles Xavier in the "X-Men" films, has died at the age of 86.

Stewart died at his home in Los Angeles in late October. According to his spokesperson, Kelly Bush Novak, he died following "a brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, conditions that had not previously been made public.

Stewart grew up in Mirfield, Yorkshire, in the north of England, in a house without a bathroom. His childhood was difficult. His father, a former army sergeant major, was violent toward his mother, an experience Stewart later wrote about in his memoir, "Making It So." He went on to become a patron of Refuge, a charity that supports victims of domestic abuse.

From an early age, Stewart was drawn to the theater. He joined an amateur drama group at the age of 12 and memorized Shakespeare as a teenager, later winning a scholarship to the Bristol Old Vic Theatre School. He then spent 14 years with the Royal Shakespeare Company, playing major roles such as Mark Antony, Henry IV and Shylock. His performance as Macbeth, which reached Broadway in 2008, earned him his only Tony Award nomination.

However, it was television that made him a global star. As Captain Picard, Stewart led the crew of the starship Enterprise for seven seasons and 178 episodes, as well as four feature films. Decades later, he returned to the role in the series "Star Trek: Picard." He also played Professor Charles Xavier, the leader of the X-Men, in a series of films, including "Logan" in 2017.

Throughout his career, Stewart continued to return to the stage. Notably, he performed Harold Pinter's "No Man's Land" and Samuel Beckett's "Waiting for Godot" alongside his close friend Ian McKellen, who later officiated at his wedding to the singer and songwriter Sunny Ozell in 2013.
Stewart was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II in 2010. He is survived by his wife and by his children, Sophia and Daniel.
Tributes poured in from across the entertainment industry. William Shatner, who played Captain Kirk in the original "Star Trek," described him as a friend, a colleague and a magnificent actor.
